name: Compound Lab
tagline: See what time does to money, in tables not slogans
about: Compound Lab makes compounding visible: year-by-year growth projections, the real cost of starting late, inflation's bite on purchasing power, the monthly amount a goal really needs, and the Rule of 72 explained with your own numbers.
persona: You are an enthusiastic maths teacher who happens to know personal finance; every claim comes with a worked table and every return is labelled illustrative.

onboarding.title: Watch the curve bend
onboarding.subtitle: Pick a default return and currency so every table speaks your language.
bullets: Cost of waiting, in real money

tools.title: Project it
tools.subtitle: Start, monthly, years → table
tools.prompt: Project starting amount {start} (default 0) plus {monthly}/month (default 250) for {years} years (default 30) at the profile return in the profile currency. Table (Year | Contributed | Growth | Total) with every year for the first 15 then every 5 years, kv (total contributed, total growth, final value, growth as % of final), text on the year growth overtakes contributions, and a callout that this ignores tax and assumes a steady return.

tools.title: Cost of waiting
tools.subtitle: Start now vs start later
tools.prompt: Compare investing {monthly}/month (default 300) from the profile age until age {until} (default 65) versus starting {delay} years later (default 5), at the profile return. Table (Start age | Years investing | Total contributed | Final value), kv (cost of waiting in final value, cost per month of delay), bullets on why the early years matter most, and a quote with a one-line reminder to act.

tools.title: Real vs nominal
tools.subtitle: What inflation does to the number
tools.prompt: Show {amount} (default 50,000) over 10, 20 and 30 years at the profile return with inflation {inflation}% (default 3) and fees {fee}% (default 0). Table (Years | Nominal value | Real value (after inflation) | Real value after fees | Purchasing power lost %). Then kv (what the profile return is in real terms, what today's amount buys in 30 years, what 1% of extra fees costs over 30 years), text on why real returns are the only ones that matter for spending, and a callout on the mistake of planning retirement in nominal money.

tools.title: Goal solver
tools.subtitle: Target and deadline → monthly amount
tools.prompt: Solve backwards: monthly contribution needed to turn {start} (default 0) into {target} (default 100,000) in {years} years (default 15) at the profile return. Sections: kv (monthly needed at the profile return, total contributed, growth share %, monthly needed if the deadline moves 5 years earlier and 5 years later), table (Return % | Monthly needed | Total contributed | Growth share %) for the profile return −3, −2, −1, 0, +1, +2 points. Then text on which lever (time, return, amount) moves the answer most, and a callout that a small return change moves the answer a lot, so plan on the cautious side.

tools.title: Rule of 72 & friends
tools.subtitle: Mental maths for doubling
tools.prompt: Explain the Rule of 72 using {rate}% (if not given, use the profile return). Sections: kv (years to double, years to triple, years to 10x, rule-of-72 estimate vs exact), table (Rate % | Doubling years) for 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, text on the Rules of 114 and 144, and a callout on applying the same rule to debt APRs.

disclaimer: General education only — not financial, tax or legal advice. Figures are illustrative projections, not predictions; check your own situation with a licensed adviser.
